name: Puru Saxena
zh_summary: $AMZN + $GOOGL reported and their stocks sold off hard. Neither is slowing the AI build. Alphabet maintained $195–205B 2026 capex guide, spending will rise significantly in 2027. Cloud revenue more than doubled. Amazon held ~$220B 2026 capex, Jassy said will spend meaningfully more next year. AWS grew 39% with 40%+ growth guided for 2027 and 2028. Market reacting to Search miss and sluggish ecommerce, and cash burn, not AI slowdown. The gap is the opportunity.
en_summary: $AMZN + $GOOGL reported and their stocks sold off hard. Neither is slowing the AI build. Alphabet maintained $195–205B 2026 capex guide, spending will rise significantly in 2027. Cloud revenue more than doubled. Amazon held ~$220B 2026 capex, Jassy said will spend meaningfully more next year. AWS grew 39% with 40%+ growth guided for 2027 and 2028. Market reacting to Search miss and sluggish ecommerce, and cash burn, not AI slowdown. The gap is the opportunity.
text:
$AMZN + $GOOGL reported and their stocks sold off hard.

Neither is slowing the AI build.

Alphabet maintained its $195–205B 2026 capex guide and said spending will rise "significantly" in 2027. Cloud revenue more than doubled.

Amazon held its ~$220B 2026 capex guide and Jassy said they will spend “meaningfully more” next year. AWS grew 39%  (fastest in nearly five years) with 40%+ growth guided for 2027 and 2028.

The market is reacting to a Search miss at Google and sluggish ecommerce growth at Amazon; and to cash burn, not to a slowdown in AI infrastructure demand.

The people building the capacity are still accelerating. The market is focused on the near-term bill. That gap is the opportunity.
orig:
$AMZN + $GOOGL reported and their stocks sold off hard.

Neither is slowing the AI build.

Amazon held its ~$220B 2026 capex guide and Jassy said they will spend “meaningfully more” next year. AWS grew 39%  (fastest in nearly five years) with 40%+ growth guided for 2027 and 2028.

The market is reacting to a Search miss at Google and sluggish ecommerce growth at Amazon; and to cash burn, not to a slowdown in AI infrastructure demand.

The people building the capacity are still accelerating. The market is focused on the near-term bill. That gap is the opportunity.

Ultimately, many continue to fail to see the improvement in the broader mkt and are putting too much stock in this minor (granted, outsized) move in Tech these last couple weeks.   Did they forget what happened Mon-Wed of this week? 

Symmetrically, QQQ bottomed Fri 10/16, it bottomed Friday 10/23 and what does it do tomorrow, 10/23? ____
Breadth & positive divergence are key.   Stay tuned.

zh_summary: Criticizes Josh Brown's bullish and simplistic views on technology earnings and stock prices, quoting his comments that earnings expectations for tech are going higher, there is an anti-bubble in technology, and Amazon $AMZN earnings could be explosive. text:
Drawdown Josh Brown's bullish, confident and remarkably simplistic soliloquy on technology earnings and stock prices this week (below) summarizes what is so wrong with Fin TV and the business media.

The investment mosaic is so much more complex than his 'glittering generalities' and singular factor views.   

Here are excerpts from his comments earlier this week on technology earnings and stock prices. @CNBC @cnbchalftime:

"Earnings expectations for tech are not coming down they are going higher.
We have an anti-bubble in technology.
When you think about the type of earnings we are going to get! 
We are going to hear from Amazon $AMZN on Thursday after the close - it could be explosive." 

Here is the full tape:
(2) Martin Pelletier on X: "Ouch. https://x.com/_Investinq/status/2115205675978834222/video/1" / X   

As I mentioned, Josh recently brought $RDDT (-$28 to $106 or -21% in after hours and -$100 in the last ten weeks or so since he recommended the name.  

@CNBC viewers have not heard any contrition and there has been no pushback by @CNBC moderator(s).

Unfortunately these are two big mistakes are not in isolation. 

I recognize that this tweet sounds ad hominem.  

I see my role is being an advocate to the retail consumer/viewer @cnbc and I am simply bringing up the facts by reiterating what he said.

If anyone at @CNBC or elsewhere on Twitter feel I am in attack mode, tell me and explain.  Unlike some, I can always learn... 

@KeithMcCullough @Hedgeye_HGRO @RPKInve
